description: A glass armonica: thirty-seven tuned bowls turn on a spindle and a wet finger rubs whichever one the pitch input names, so notes take time to speak and keep ringing after the gate drops

params.text: Sets how fast the bowls turn, 0 to 6Hz, which sets how quickly a rubbed bowl comes up to level
Attenuverts the rotation CV before it is added to the rotation knob
Sets how wet the finger is: dry gives a bright squeaking excitation, wet a dark smooth one
Attenuverts the water CV before it is added to the water knob
Sets how long a bowl keeps ringing after its gate drops, despite the panel printing DECAY
Attenuverts the sustain CV before it is added to the sustain knob
Darkens the bowls, from a bright transparent ring at one end of the travel to a muted one at the other
Attenuverts the damp CV before it is added to the damp knob
Wobbles the spindle, which sets how much tremolo the rubbing produces
Attenuverts the wobble CV before it is added to the wobble knob
Damps every bowl at once while it is held, at the depth set by the Damper Depth slider on the menu
Places the bowls across the stereo pair, -1 to 1, from reversed through mono to fully spread
Bends the pitch of every bowl continuously, -1 to 1, which detunes them away from their fixed tuning
Attenuverts the FM CV before it is added to the FM knob
Sets the output level, silence to four times, which drives the output saturator at the top of its travel
Attenuverts the volume CV before it is added to the volume knob
Sets how hard the external input excites the bowls, silence to full
Attenuverts the external gain CV before it is added to the external gain knob

inputs.text: Picks which bowl is rubbed, as a volt per octave folded into the three octaves the bowls cover; the number of channels here is how many notes can sound at once
A high gate keeps the matching bowl being rubbed; with nothing patched every channel of the pitch input holds its bowl continuously, so the damper is the only way to stop a note
Sets how hard each bowl is rubbed, 0-10V per channel, matched channel for channel with the pitch input
A high gate damps the bowl of the matching pitch channel, silencing that note while leaving the others alone
Changes the rotation speed, scaled by a tenth and added to the rotation knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to 0 to 6Hz
Changes the wetness of the finger, scaled by a tenth and added to the water knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's travel
Changes the ring-off time, scaled by a tenth and added to the sustain knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's travel
Changes the brightness, scaled by a tenth and added to the damp knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's travel
Changes the spindle wobble, scaled by a tenth and added to the wobble knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's travel
Changes the continuous detune, scaled by a tenth and added to the FM knob through its attenuverter
Changes the output level, scaled by a tenth and added to the volume knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's travel
A voltage above 0.5V damps every bowl at once, which is what the damp button does by hand
A signal fed into every ringing bowl, which lets them be excited by something other than the rubbing
Changes how hard the external input excites the bowls, scaled by a tenth and added to the external gain knob through its attenuverter
Transposes every bowl, added to the root knob and clamped to two octaves either way

outputs.text: The left side of the bowls as panned by the spread control, soft-clipped and clamped to -12 to 12V
The right side of the bowls as panned by the spread control, soft-clipped and clamped to -12 to 12V
Follows the loudness of the mixed output as a root-mean-square envelope, 0-10V

notes: nothing sounds until a pitch arrives at V/OCT; with no gate patched that pitch alone keeps its bowl sounding, and the DAMP ALL button or the mute gate is what stops it
the bowls are fixed at thirty-seven tuned pitches over three octaves, and the pitch input is folded into that range and snapped to the nearest bowl; ROOT and FM move the tuning
menu: Attack — a slider setting how quickly a bowl's pressure envelope rises once its gate goes high
Release — a slider setting how quickly a bowl's pressure envelope falls once its gate drops
Attack Curve (log - exp) — a slider from -1 to 1 bending the pressure envelope's rise between logarithmic and exponential
Release Curve (log - exp) — a slider from -1 to 1 bending the pressure envelope's fall between logarithmic and exponential
Max Noise Cutoff Hz (dry setting) — a slider from 100Hz to 4000Hz setting how bright the rubbing noise is with the water control fully dry
Damper Depth (gate/mute darkness) — a slider setting how far the damper closes the bowls down, from a light touch to a full stop
Panic: Clear All Bowl Energy — silences every bowl at once, which clears a runaway build-up without reloading the patch
